general: Extract every entity of the supplied types. Return exact spans from the query. Leave other text unlabelled.

classes.name: Event
classes.description: Refers to a significant occurrence or happening.
rules: EV1 Such as wars, conferences, festivals, sport events, etc.
EV2 Examples: "World War II", "Cannes Film Festival", "47th Berlin International Film Festival", "Luge at the 1976 Winter Olympics", "Equestrian at the 1976 Summer Olympics".

classes.name: Person
classes.description: Refers to an individual's name that is not a writer.
rules: PE1 Person is only for people not known for writing, such as actors, fictional characters and rulers: "Ingrid Bergman", "Jack Ryan", "Sennacherib".
PE2 Examples: "Lindbergh", "Giacomo di Benincasa", "Baron Cohen", "Emperor Toghon Temür", "Princess Noguk".

classes.name: Location
classes.description: Refers to a specific geographical or structural location.
rules: LO1 This includes but is not limited to: places (e.g., parks, landmarks), bridges, cities, towns, villages, areas and other distinct regions.
LO2 Examples: "London", "Chalcedon", "Charles Dickens Museum", "Charles Dickens Birthplace Museum", "Portsmouth".

classes.name: Book
classes.description: Refers to a published work of literature, typically consisting of written content bound in a physical or digital format.
rules: BO1 Films and TV series are Other, not Book, even when they share a novel's title: "Citizen Kane", "Vertigo", "Sling Blade", "The Darjeeling Limited".
BO2 Examples: "The Plague of Doves", "A History of Warfare", "The Color Purple", "Rabbit at Rest", "The Fountainhead".

classes.name: Magazine
classes.description: Refers to a periodical publication that features articles, stories, and various literary works.
rules: MA1 Examples: "The New Yorker", "Simbolul", "Private Eye", "The Atlantic", "The Crisis".

classes.name: Country
rules: CO1 Nationality, people and language words are Other, not Country: "American", "British", "English", "Roman".
CO2 Examples: "Germany", "Han dynasty", "England", "Italy", "Yuan dynasty".

classes.name: Writer
classes.description: Refers to an individual actively engaged in the creation of literary works, including writers, novelists, scriptwriters, poets, and other literary artists.
rules: WR1 If a person is involved in literature-related roles, annotate them as a writer entity instead of a person entity.

WR2 A person known for writing is a Writer: novelists, poets, playwrights, screenwriters, journalists, critics, historians, philosophers and other authors, even when the sentence is about something else and even for a bare surname: "Guillaume Apollinaire", "Herodotus", "Emily Brontë", "Elkin".
WR3 When unsure whether a person is a Writer or a Person, choose Writer.
WR4 Examples: "John Keegan", "Leo Tolstoy", "John Steinbeck", "Yeats", "Jacobs".

classes.name: Poem
classes.description: Refers to a literary composition characterized by its structured form, rhythm, and often heightened language.
rules: PO1 A single poem, including a long, epic or narrative poem or a ballad, is Poem, not Book: "The Raggedy Man", "Divine Comedy", "The Tyger".
PO2 Examples: "Barbara Frietchie", "The Barefoot Boy", "Maud Muller", "Snow-Bound", "Shishupala Vadha".

classes.name: Award
classes.description: Refers to a recognition or honor bestowed upon individuals or works of literature for notable achievements.
rules: AW1 An Award span keeps the category after "for": "Hugo Award for Novella", "Booker Prize for fiction", "Volpi Cup for Best Actor"; it stops before "for" when the title of a work follows.
AW2 Examples: "Pulitzer Prize", "Nebula Award", "Hugo Award", "Academy Awards", "Nobel Prize in Literature".

classes.name: Organization
classes.description: Refers to a structured group, institution, company, or association.
rules: OR1 This category covers a diverse range of organizations, including businesses, non-profits, educational institutions, and government agencies.
OR2 Examples: "Science Fiction and Fantasy Writers of America", "The New York Times", "New York Times", "Food52", "Amnesty International".

classes.name: LiteraryGenre
classes.description: Refers to categories in literature defined by unique artistic techniques, themes, content, and lengths.
rules: LG1 Label words such as poetry, essay or novel as well as content categories like Science Fiction, Fantasy, and Fiction.
LG2 It also encompasses culturally influenced genres, such as Nordic countries poetry.
LG3 Label every literary form or genre word, also as a plain common noun after his, her or the: "novel", "novels", "poem", "poems", "short story", "prose".
LG4 Keep genre adjectives in the span ("dystopian novel", "science fiction novel", "high fantasy novels") but not ordinals or words like last: in "his seventh novel" label only "novel".
LG5 Examples: "poem", "poems", "novels", "novel", "science fiction".

classes.name: Other
classes.description: Refers to named entities that are not included in any other category.
rules: OT1 Nationality, people, religious and language words are Other: "American", "Swedish", "Jewish", "Germans".
OT2 Examples: "American", "British", "English", "French", "Goryeo".
